segments.text: Jay runs into Cameron while having lunch with some old friends. Instead of introducing him as Mitchell’s partner, Jay calls him “a friend of my son.” Mitchell is upset because he and Cameron have been together for five years and are raising a daughter together.

segments.text: Mitchell confronts Jay, but Jay says his friends wouldn’t understand. To make him question his attitude, Mitchell claims that Jay’s friend Shorty is gay. He isn’t, but Mitchell is so confident that Jay starts wondering whether it could be true.

segments.text: Gloria also thinks Shorty might be gay and encourages Jay to talk to him. Jay takes Shorty golfing and awkwardly tells him that he can share his secret. Shorty finally admits that he’s hiding something: he owes a dangerous gambler twenty thousand dollars.

segments.text: Meanwhile, Phil installs a complicated universal remote for the family’s home theater. Claire can’t use it and becomes angry because Phil always explains technology to her like she’s a child. She loses her temper and breaks the remote.

segments.text: At Jay and Gloria’s house, Manny is preparing for a date with Whitney, someone he met through an online book club. He expects a girl his age, but Whitney turns out to be a grown woman who also thought Manny was an adult.

segments.text: The date clearly isn’t going anywhere, but Gloria feels sorry for Whitney and gives her a makeover. Whitney becomes much more confident. When Cameron arrives later, they immediately connect over fashion, old movies, and vampire books.

segments.text: By the end, everyone changes a little. Jay tries to be more accepting, Claire learns to use the remote, and Whitney feels better about herself. They don’t change completely, but sometimes fifteen percent is enough.
